"Here are the functions of **BonziBuddy**, **Clippy (Clippit)**, and **Merlin**, followed by an explanation of how BonziBuddy’s sprite/animation system worked.

## BonziBuddy functions

BonziBuddy was a standalone Windows desktop assistant built on Microsoft Agent. Its user-facing features were entertainment, speech, basic productivity, and web/download assistance. 

- **Talk and read text aloud:** It used the Lernout @COMMENT_BODY@ Hauspie/Microsoft Speech API “Sydney” voice (also called “Adult Male #2”) to speak typed text. 
- **Tell jokes and facts:** It had built-in joke, trivia, and fact content. 
- **Sing songs:** It could perform songs using its speech and animation features. 
- **Manage downloads:** It offered a download-management feature. 
- **Calendar and scheduling help:** It included basic organizer/calendar assistance, such as reminders and appointments. 
- **Web-search assistance:** It could help users search the web. 
- **Email assistance:** It could notify users of new messages and read email aloud. 
- **Desktop animations:** Bonzi could perform idle and attention-getting animations, such as riding a surfboard, swinging on a vine, eating bananas, wearing sunglasses, or sleeping. 
- **Paid content and upgrades:** Bonzi Software sold add-ons for additional jokes, facts, songs, and speech-recognition features. 
- **Adware/spyware functions:** It served ads, installed a browser toolbar, reset the browser homepage to Bonzi.com, prompted for/tracked user information, and was associated with deceptive ads imitating Windows alerts. 

## Clippy / Office Assistant functions

“Clippy” is the public name for **Clippit**, the default Office Assistant in Microsoft Office. The Office Assistant was not a general Windows assistant; it was an Office help interface that connected users to help content and Office features. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)

- **Offer contextual help:** It appeared when Office decided the user might need help with a task, wizard, or feature. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)
- **Detect document patterns:** For example, typing an address followed by “Dear” could trigger: “It looks like you’re writing a letter. Would you like help?” [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)
- **Launch wizards:** It could point users toward Office wizards for tasks such as letters, documents, and other Office workflows. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)
- **Search Help:** It interfaced with Office help content and could help users find relevant help topics. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)
- **Give tips and shortcuts:** It presented productivity tips and keyboard shortcuts. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)
- **Advise on Office features:** It suggested more effective ways to use Office features. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)
- **Speak and accept speech:** Microsoft Agent-based Office Assistants could use TruVoice text-to-speech for output and, where supported, Microsoft’s speech-recognition engine for input. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)
- **Use different characters:** Clippit was the default, but users could choose other Office Assistants, including The Dot, Genius, Hoverbot, Kairu, Office Logo, Mother Nature, Power Pup, Scribble, Will, F1, Links, Rocky, and Merlin. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)

## Merlin functions

Merlin was a Microsoft-provided Microsoft Agent character—a wizard character—not an Office Assistant with a separate feature set. His capabilities came from the Microsoft Agent platform and the application that used him. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)

- **Appear as an animated desktop character:** Merlin could be displayed on top of applications or web pages. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)
- **Speak through text-to-speech:** Microsoft Agent supported SAPI-based text-to-speech output. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)
- **Accept speech input:** Where a compatible speech-recognition engine was installed, Agent characters could accept spoken commands. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)
- **Perform scripted animations:** Developers could trigger animations, gestures, movements, and character actions through Microsoft Agent. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)
- **Show speech balloons:** Agent characters could display text in a balloon while speaking. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)
- **Assist within an application or webpage:** Developers embedded Merlin in programs or Internet Explorer webpages using ActiveX, VBScript, or Visual Basic for Applications. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)
- **Serve as a Windows XP search companion:** Microsoft Agent characters, including Merlin, were used in Windows XP’s search-companion interface. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)
- **Guide users through tasks:** In practice, developers used Merlin for tutorials, navigation help, notifications, prompts, and interactive presentations; those behaviors depended on the host program’s script. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)

## How BonziBuddy sprite animation worked

BonziBuddy’s “spriteing” was not modern sprite-sheet animation in the usual game-engine sense. It used **Microsoft Agent character files**, which stored a character’s visual frames, animation definitions, speech-balloon behavior, and interaction data. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)

### The character files

Microsoft Agent characters were packaged as:

- **.ACS files:** A compiled character file containing the character and its animations.
- **.ACF plus .ACA files:** A format intended for web distribution, with one animation stored per `.ACA` file. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)
- **.ACD files:** Character-definition source files created in Microsoft’s Agent Character Editor. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BonziBuddy)

Bonzi’s purple gorilla was therefore a Microsoft Agent character asset: a set of drawn poses/frames plus instructions telling the runtime when to show each pose, move the character, play sound, display a balloon, and return to an idle pose.

### How an animation played

A typical Bonzi animation worked like this:

1. **Trigger:** The user clicked Bonzi, selected a menu action, or the program triggered an idle animation.
2. **Command:** BonziBuddy called the Microsoft Agent runtime and requested an animation by name, such as a wave, dance, surf, sleep, or attention-getting animation.
3. **Frame sequence:** The Agent runtime displayed the character’s pre-made frames in order, creating the illusion of motion.
4. **Positioning:** The runtime placed the character at a desktop coordinate, often near the taskbar or another screen location.
5. **Speech sync:** If the character spoke, the runtime displayed a speech balloon and synchronized mouth frames with the TTS voice.
6. **Return state:** After the animation, Bonzi returned to an idle pose or disappeared until the next trigger.

### Why it looked choppy

The animations were **frame-based**, not fully 3D-rendered or continuously animated. Bonzi had a limited library of poses and transitions, so actions such as surfing, swinging, eating, or sleeping were short loops or sequences of hand-drawn frames. 

That is why Bonzi’s movement had the distinctive late-1990s look: exaggerated poses, abrupt transitions, simple looping motion, and a cartoon character pasted over the Windows desktop.

### Bonzi versus Clippy and Merlin

| Assistant | Main role | Animation approach | Typical behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BonziBuddy** | Standalone entertainment/productivity assistant | Microsoft Agent character animations, plus Bonzi-specific poses and speech | Jokes, songs, speech, downloads, calendar help, web assistance, ads |
| **Clippit / Clippy** | Office help assistant | Office Assistant character with Agent-based animation from Office 2000 onward | Contextual Office help, wizards, tips, shortcuts |
| **Merlin** | Reusable Microsoft Agent character | Microsoft Agent animation and speech system | Whatever the host app or webpage scripted: help, tutorials, prompts, search companion |

In short: **Bonzi’s sprite work was Microsoft Agent animation**, while **Clippy’s sprite work was Office Assistant animation**, and **Merlin’s sprite work was the general Microsoft Agent animation system**. BonziBuddy added its own gorilla character, scripts, sounds, and feature menus on top of that platform. [en.wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant)

Attachments:
- [Bonzi.7z](https://omgithub.com/api/issue-attachments/92a5a1ec-7e20-4230-87a1-473e4ea978a8)
- [Bonzi_assets.7z](https://omgithub.com/api/issue-attachments/a8c1516f-1b3c-4513-89e7-bacc2177d61d)

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

### Result
Total messages: 0 (Errors: 0, Warnings: 0)

Built **Agent Rush**, a playable retro desktop arcade in `index.html`.

Route 12 incoming requests to Bonzi, Clippit, or Merlin. Earn points and streak bonuses for correct matches; the shift ends when time runs out or you make three mistakes. Start with **Let’s Go**, then click an answer or use keys **1–3**. Sound is optional.

The game uses original in-page character illustrations and animation, with no tracking, toolbars, or real downloads. I checked the page in a browser, verified a correct answer scores and advances the queue, and confirmed there were no JavaScript errors.
